# The miniapp SDK

<!-- Generated by `bun run sdk:render` from src/sdk/contract.ts. Edit the contract, not this file. -->

window.miniapp is the only host surface a Capsule has, in the editor preview and on every Deployment. Each module is a namespace on it. A published call is one or more MCP tool calls to the Deployment's runtime endpoint with the app session cookie.

```js
const session = await miniapp.auth.session();                    // { userId, name, role }; role is "anonymous" when signed out
await miniapp.auth.signIn();                                     // published login page, preview selects Alice
await miniapp.auth.signOut();                                    // revoke this app session
const rows = await miniapp.actions.call("tasks.list");           // array of row objects
await miniapp.actions.call("tasks.create", { title });           // { changes, lastInsertId }
await miniapp.actions.call("lesson.finish", { lesson });         // a signal action: { recorded: true }
const files = await miniapp.files.list();                        // that user's private files, plus public files
const stored = await miniapp.files.upload(file);                 // private to the signed-in user
const shared = await miniapp.files.upload(file, { visibility: "public" });
image.src = await miniapp.files.url(photo.file_id);              // "/_littlebox/files/<id>"
const text = await (await fetch(await miniapp.files.url(note.id))).text();
await miniapp.files.update(draft.id, { visibility: "public" });  // the draft is now published under the same ID
await miniapp.files.delete(note.file_id);                        // { id, deleted: true }
```

There is nothing else: no fetch to other origins, no localStorage contract, no miniapp.db and no SQL from the browser, no miniapp.track and no analytics call: a Signal is declared on a Server Action and recorded when miniapp.actions.call runs it.

Error messages below are the exact text a published app receives as `error.message`. The Editor preview column says where the preview in the editor answers differently.

## Refusals on every call

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Sign in to use Littlebox MCP.` | the Deployment is private and the visitor has no session; actions.call then sends the browser to /_littlebox/login and auth.session returns the anonymous state instead | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Deployment not found.` | the host name matches no Deployment | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Cross-origin or unrecognized-host MCP request rejected.` | the request does not come from the Deployment's own origin | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `MCP request exceeds 200 KB.` | one request body is larger than 200,000 bytes | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Invalid MCP response.` | the response does not answer the request the SDK sent | SDK | Never refuses |

## miniapp.auth

Who is using the app. The Kernel owns accounts and sessions; the app only reads the current one.

- Visibility decides who may open the app shell. It never grants data access on its own.
- The Deployment's Signup Policy, which the owner sets in the editor or with signup_policy_set, decides who may create an account: Open, Invitation only, Closed or an Allowlist. Under Invitation only, the sign-in page offers no account creation; invited people accept from the link in their email, which opens /_littlebox/invitation.

### miniapp.auth.session()

Read the signed-in Runtime Actor, or the anonymous state so the app can show a sign-in button.

Signed-out visitors on a public Deployment: allowed.

Runtime MCP tools: `auth_session`.

Returns { userId, name, role }. Signed in, name is the account email and role is "member" or "owner". Signed out, { userId: "anonymous", name: "Anonymous", role: "anonymous" }.

Editor preview: Returns Alice or Bob, the preview's test accounts, with role "member", or the anonymous state.

### miniapp.auth.signIn()

Send the visitor to the Deployment's login page at /_littlebox/login.

Signed-out visitors on a public Deployment: allowed.

Runtime MCP tools: none.

Returns nothing; the page navigates away.

Editor preview: Signs in as Alice without leaving the page and returns her session.

### miniapp.auth.signOut()

Revoke this app session, clear its cookie and release the file URLs the SDK created.

Signed-out visitors on a public Deployment: refused.

Runtime MCP tools: `auth_logout`.

Returns { ok: true }.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `authentication-required` | no one is signed in | Kernel | Never refuses |

Editor preview: Switches to the signed-out state and returns the anonymous session.

## miniapp.actions

The only door to the database. A call names a Server Action declared in actions.json and passes its input; the Kernel authorizes the caller, binds the input and runs the action's one SQL statement, or records its Signal.

- A query action returns the rows of its SELECT. Column names are exactly the ones the SELECT projects, so alias any expression the app reads.
- A mutation action returns { changes, lastInsertId }. Read changed rows with a separate query. A mutation that declares a guard and changes no row is refused with the guard instead.
- The Action Contract, action-contract.json, lists every action with its inputs, the columns it returns, its errors and limits. It is written from actions.json and schema.sql by littlebox contract and carried in the export; an expression the SELECT returns without AS has no name in it, and the Validation Gate warns.
- To record that something happened, such as a signup to a newsletter or a finished lesson, declare a signal on the mutation that does it, or add an action of kind signal and call it with miniapp.actions.call. There is no other tracking call.
- A call the Kernel refuses records no Signal and counts in no Usage total, except a guard's refusal, which Usage counts under refused.

Declared with `signal` in `actions.json`. { "name": "order.placed", "properties"?: ["input binding keys", "actor"] } on a mutation, or on an action of "kind": "signal" that has access and bindings but no statement. When the action succeeds, and for a mutation only when it changed at least one row, the Kernel records the Signal with the named inputs as its properties, in the Deployment's Usage store. The property actor records the caller's ID: the user's, the API key's, or null for a visitor or a signed request. A signal action runs no SQL and returns { recorded: true }. The owner reads Signals with signals_read; the app cannot. The Validation Gate and the Kernel refuse the same declarations with the same messages.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Action <name> is a query, so it cannot declare a signal. Declare it on a mutation or on a "kind": "signal" action.` | the action is a query | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> names signal property <key>, which is not one of its input bindings.` | a property is not the key of an input binding; actor, kernel and literal bindings have no key | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> names signal property <key> twice.` | properties lists a key twice | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> names signal property actor, which records the caller's ID, and also has an input named actor. Rename the input.` | properties lists actor and an input binding's key is actor | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> names more than 8 signal properties.` | properties lists more than 8 keys | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> names an invalid signal. Use dot-separated lowercase words, such as "order.placed", up to 64 characters.` | the name has one word, a capital, a space, an empty part or more than 64 characters | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> has an invalid signal declaration.` | signal is not an object, has a key other than name and properties, has no name, or properties is not a list of strings | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> is a signal action, so it must declare a signal.` | the kind is signal and there is no signal key | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> is a signal action, so it runs no SQL and cannot declare a statement.` | the kind is signal and the action has a statement | Kernel | Same |

Limits:

- 8 properties per Signal; a string property keeps its first 128 bytes
- a signal action counts toward the action limit like any other action
- a signal action cannot declare http
- a mutation that changed no row records no Signal
- the Kernel keeps the newest 50,000 Signals per Deployment and drops the oldest

Declared with `guard` in `actions.json`. "guard": "<message>" on a mutation. When its statement changes no row, the Kernel refuses the call with that message instead of answering { changes: 0, lastInsertId: 0 }: a tool error for miniapp.actions.call, 403 on an HTTP route. Usage counts the call under refused, and no Signal is recorded. Write the app's rule into the statement's WHERE, such as "the caller is an organizer" or "the slot is free", and the guard is what the person sees when the rule says no. Without a guard a mutation answers { changes: 0 } as before. The Validation Gate and the Kernel refuse the same declarations with the same messages.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Action <name> is a query, so it cannot declare a guard. Declare it on a mutation.` | the action is a query | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> is a signal action, so it cannot declare a guard. Declare it on a mutation.` | the action is a signal action | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> has an invalid guard. Use a message of 1 to 200 characters on one line.` | guard is not a string, is empty or blank, is longer than 200 characters, or holds a line break or another control character | Kernel | Same |

Limits:

- a guard is 1 to 200 characters on one line

### miniapp.actions.call(name, input = {})

Invoke one declared Server Action as the current Runtime Actor.

Signed-out visitors on a public Deployment: allowed.

Runtime MCP tools: `actions_invoke`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | Yes | A Server Action name declared in actions.json, e.g. tasks.list |
| `input` | `object` | No | One value per input binding of the action, keyed by the binding's key. Defaults to {} |

Returns an array of row objects for a query action, { changes, lastInsertId } for a mutation action, { recorded: true } for a signal action, { callId, queued: true } for a call action.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Server action not declared.` | actions.json declares no action with that name | Kernel | Same |
| `authentication-required` | the action is not declared anonymous and no one is signed in; the published SDK also sends the browser to /_littlebox/login | Kernel | Same |
| `rate-limited` | more than 30 calls in 10 seconds from one signed-out client address on one Deployment, or 120 from one signed-in user | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Arguments must be an object.` | input is not an object, e.g. null | Kernel | Same |
| `Expected a string.` | name is not a string | Kernel | Same |
| `Unexpected action input: <key>` | input has a key no input binding declares | Kernel | Same |
| `This action requires an authenticated actor.` | an anonymous action binds the actor id and no one is signed in | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> answers only on its HTTP route, <key>.` | the action's route does not answer anyone: it declares a signature or callers, or it has no signature on a private Deployment. The preview refuses the first two only, since it has no visibility | Kernel | Same |
| `Missing action input: <key>` | a required input is omitted | Kernel | Same |
| `<key> must be a non-empty string.` | a string input is not a string, or is empty or only whitespace | Kernel | Same |
| `<key> is too long.` | a string input is longer than its maxLength in UTF-16 code units | Kernel | Same |
| `<key> must be a number.` | a number input is not a JSON number | Kernel | Same |
| `<key> must be a boolean.` | a boolean input is not true or false | Kernel | Same |
| `Query result exceeds 2 MiB or 1000 rows.` | a query produces more than 1000 rows or more than 2 MiB of JSON | Kernel | Same |
| `This app reached its limit of calls in the last minute. Try again in a minute.` | the action is a call and the app queued 20 calls in the last 60 seconds, or the number the installation set | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Action <name> runs only after the call <key> answers.` | the action is the then mutation of a call, which only the Kernel runs | Kernel | Same |

Limits:

- 30 calls per 10 seconds per signed-out client address and Deployment; 120 per 10 seconds per signed-in user
- 1000 rows and 2 MiB per query result
- 2 seconds per statement; SQLite's own error text is returned when a statement fails or runs out of time
- string inputs default to a maxLength of 10,000 UTF-16 code units
- 256 MiB per app database

Editor preview: Ignores the Deployment's visibility and rate limits, and keeps its database in the browser with a 10 MiB cap. A signal action returns { recorded: true } and records nothing; Signals exist only on a Deployment or a Development Kernel. A call action returns { callId, queued: true } and sends nothing; only a Kernel sends calls.

## miniapp.files

Small files stored by the Kernel for one Deployment. A file is private to the user who uploaded it unless the upload asked for public.

- Only the uploader can list or read a private file.
- On a public Deployment a signed-out visitor can list and read public files. On a private Deployment any signed-in user can.
- files.list and files.upload download over MCP, check the SHA-256 and return a Blob URL. The page's policy allows connect-src 'self' only, so fetch cannot read a Blob URL again. To fetch a file, or to show one without downloading every file, use files.url. It returns the file's path GET /_littlebox/files/<id> on the app's own origin, which img, fetch and a link all reach.
- The uploader alone changes a file's visibility with files.update or deletes it with files.delete. A deleted file stops counting against the 20 MiB quota and its ID answers File not found from then on, through every door.
- A visitor without a session on a private Deployment is asked to sign in before any file is looked up: 401 authentication-required. On a public Deployment, a file the visitor may not read answers 404 File not found, the same as a missing one. A signed-in user who may not read a file also gets 404.

### miniapp.files.list()

List and download every file the current actor may read.

Signed-out visitors on a public Deployment: allowed.

Runtime MCP tools: `files_list`, `files_read`, `transfer_read`, `transfer_cancel`.

Returns an array of { id, name, type, size, visibility, createdAt, ownerId, url }. ownerId is present only on files the caller uploaded. url is a Blob URL; it keeps the type for image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp and image/avif and is application/octet-stream otherwise.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `File not found.` | the file was removed or the actor may not read it | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Too many active transfers. Cancel completed transfers before starting another.` | the actor already holds 2 transfers, or the Deployment holds 32 | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Transfer not found or expired.` | a transfer outlived its 10 minutes | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Invalid file size.` | the Kernel announced a size outside 0 to 2 MiB | SDK | Never refuses |
| `Invalid file block.` | a downloaded block does not continue at the expected offset or exceeds 64 KiB | SDK | Never refuses |
| `File checksum mismatch.` | the downloaded bytes do not match the SHA-256 the Kernel announced | SDK | Never refuses |

Limits:

- every listed file is downloaded, one at a time, on each call
- 2 MiB per file

Editor preview: Reads files from browser storage and returns data URLs.

### miniapp.files.upload(file, options)

Store a File or Blob for the signed-in user and return it as files.list would.

Signed-out visitors on a public Deployment: refused.

Runtime MCP tools: `transfer_begin`, `transfer_write`, `transfer_complete`, `files_upload`, `transfer_cancel`, `files_read`, `transfer_read`.

| `file` | `File \| Blob` | Yes | The bytes to store, with its name and type |
| `options.visibility` | `"private" \| "public"` | No | "private", the default, keeps the file to the uploader. Pass "public" only when every visitor of a public app may read the bytes. Any other value is refused before the upload starts |

Returns { id, name, type, size, visibility, createdAt, ownerId, url }. ownerId is present only on files the caller uploaded. url is a Blob URL; it keeps the type for image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp and image/avif and is application/octet-stream otherwise.

| `Transfer size is outside the limit.` | the file is empty or larger than 2 MiB | Kernel | Same |
| `This deployment has reached its 20 MiB file quota.` | the Deployment's files would exceed 20 MiB together | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `File not found.` | the file was removed or the actor may not read it | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Too many active transfers. Cancel completed transfers before starting another.` | the actor already holds 2 transfers, or the Deployment holds 32 | Kernel | Never refuses |

- 20 MiB of files per Deployment

## The calls module, declared, with no browser call

Calls from this app to another app or an outside service, made by the Kernel from its own process, never from the browser. There is no browser call: the page invokes the call action with miniapp.actions.call, which answers { callId, queued: true }, and the Kernel sends the request, retries it and runs the then mutation with the answer.

- The Kernel resolves an outside host once per attempt and refuses it when any address it resolves to is loopback, private, link-local (where cloud metadata answers), shared, documentation, benchmarking, multicast, reserved, unspecified, unique-local, or an IPv4 address carried in IPv6. It then connects to the address it checked, so a second DNS answer cannot redirect the request.
- http is allowed only to an app of this installation, which the Kernel reaches in its own process. Every other URL must be https.
- Each attempt of a signed call signs again with a new nonce, so a retry is never refused as a replay.
- A paused app sends no call and runs no then mutation until its pause ends.
- Usage counts each queued call under call, by action. The then mutation counts as an action, or under refused when its guard refuses, and records its Signal with actor null.
- The editor preview answers { callId, queued: true } and sends nothing. Run calls on a Development Kernel with littlebox dev, or on a Deployment.

Declared with `kind: call` in `actions.json`. { "kind": "call", "access", "bindings": [input bindings only], "method": "GET" | "POST", "url": "https://inbox-2.apps.example.org/hooks/events", "body"?: { "<body key>": "<input key>" }, "auth"?: { "secret": "<name>", "header"?: "X-Inbox-Signature" } | { "key": "<name>" }, "then"?: { "action": "<mutation>", "inputs": { "<input key>": "<JSON pointer>" } } }. A POST sends the body keys as a JSON object and a GET as query parameters after the URL's own; a null or missing input leaves its key out. auth.secret signs the request with Littlebox's route scheme in the header, X-Littlebox-Signature unless header names another; auth.key sends the secret's value, an API key, as Authorization: Bearer. The secret's value stays in the Kernel; it never reaches the browser, the artifact or an export. When the call ends, delivered or failed, the then mutation runs once with no actor, its inputs read by JSON pointers from { ok, status, error, body, input }: ok is true for a 2xx answer, status the HTTP status or null, error the Kernel's error kind or null, body the answer parsed as JSON or null, and input the call's own inputs. A then mutation runs only after its call. A URL whose host is an app of this installation goes through that app's route code in the Kernel's process, with the same callers check, signature check, guard, Usage and Signal. The owner reads every call with calls_read. The Validation Gate and the Kernel refuse the same declarations with the same messages, except the three marked as the Kernel's alone.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Action <name> is a call, so it runs no SQL and cannot declare a statement, a signal, a guard or an http route.` | a call declares a statement, signal, guard or http | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> is a <key>, so it cannot declare url, method, body, auth or then. Those keys belong to an action of "kind": "call".` | a query, mutation or signal action declares a call's keys | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> is a call, so its bindings may only be inputs.` | a call binds the actor, the time or a literal; the Kernel adds no identity or clock to a request that leaves the app | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> must call with "method": "GET" or "POST".` | method is missing, lowercase or another verb | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> has an invalid url. Use an absolute https:// URL without credentials or a fragment, up to 2048 characters.` | url is missing, relative, not http or https, carries a user or password, a fragment, a space or a control character, or is longer than 2048 characters | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> calls the IP address <key>. Name a host instead.` | the host is an IPv4 or IPv6 address, in any notation | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> calls <key>, which names this machine or a cloud metadata service.` | the host is localhost, metadata, instance-data or a name under .internal | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> calls a path under /_littlebox, /oauth, /.well-known or /mcp, which belong to the Kernel.` | the URL's first path segment is reserved, in any letter case | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> has an invalid body. Map each body key to one of the call's input keys, at most 32.` | body is not an object, has more than 32 keys, a key that is not 1 to 64 letters, digits, _, . or -, or a value that is not a string | Kernel | Same |

| `Action <name> reads <key> for then, but <key> is not one of its input bindings.` | a pointer under /input names an input the call does not have | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> names <name> as its then, which is not declared.` | the then action is not in actions.json | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> names <name> as its then, which is not a mutation.` | the then action is a query, a signal action or a call | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> names <name> as its then, which answers on an HTTP route. A then mutation runs only after its call.` | the then mutation declares http | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> names <name> as its then, which binds the actor. A then mutation runs with no caller.` | the then mutation has an actor binding | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> fills <key>, which is not an input of <name>.` | then.inputs names a key the mutation has no input binding for | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> leaves <key> of <name> unfilled. Fill it from the answer or make the input nullable.` | a required input of the then mutation has no pointer | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> calls http://<key>, which is not an app of this installation. Use https.` | publishing an http URL whose host is not under the installation's host suffix; the editor cannot see the installation, so only the Kernel refuses this | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Action <name> calls <key>, the editor's host. A call reaches an app or an outside service, never the editor.` | publishing a URL on the installation's own host or its MCP host; only the Kernel refuses this | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Action <name> calls with the secret <name>, which is not set for this project. Set it with secret_set before publishing.` | publishing, and the owner has not set the secret auth names; only the Kernel refuses this | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Action <name> signs its route with the secret <name>, which is set for calls only. Set a route secret with a value of its own.` | publishing a route whose signature names a secret set with use call | Kernel | Never refuses |

Limits:

- 20 calls queued per app in any 60 seconds, unless the installation sets LITTLEBOX_CALLS_PER_MINUTE
- 10 seconds per attempt, from connecting to the last byte of the answer
- 64 KiB per answer; a larger one ends the call as failed with answer-too-large
- 5 attempts for a network failure, a timeout, 408, 425, 429 or a 5xx, waiting 30 seconds, then 1, 2 and 4 minutes; any other answer is final
- no redirect is followed: a 3xx is the answer
- the outbox keeps the newest 1000 finished calls per app and the first 1 KiB of each answer

Declared with `connects` in `manifest`. "connects": ["https://api.example.com"] in the project manifest, or project.manifest.connects in littlebox.json. Each origin is added to the page's connect-src, so the page may fetch it directly: another app's public GET route, which answers with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, or an outside API that allows the app's origin. Nothing else is loosened. A key or a secret never goes to the browser: a request that needs one is a call action, which the Kernel sends.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `connects must be a list of at most 10 origins, such as ["https://api.example.com"].` | connects is not a list of strings or lists more than 10 | Kernel | Same |
| `connects lists <key>, which is not an origin. Write it as https://host or https://host:port, with no path; http only for a host under localhost.` | an entry is not exactly an origin: http to a host outside localhost, a path or trailing slash, a wildcard, capitals, or the default port written out | Kernel | Same |
| `connects lists <key> twice.` | an origin appears twice | Kernel | Same |

Limits:

- 10 origins

## The http module, declared, with no browser call

Routes on the Deployment's own host for programs and other services: a JSON endpoint, a webhook, a file a program fetches. There is no browser call; the app's own pages keep using miniapp.actions.call, and may use a file's route as an img src.

- Only an action declared anonymous may bind a route. A route has three kinds of caller: a service that signs the request (signature), a program that sends Authorization: Bearer with an API key the owner issued (key), and a person signed in to the app, from the app's own origin (session). An actor binding yields the key's ID or the user's ID; a signed request has no actor.
- Without callers, a signed route takes the signature or a key, an unsigned route on a private app a key or a session, and an unsigned route on a public app anyone. A person whose session the route does not take must sign like any sender.
- An action whose route does not answer anyone answers only on that route: miniapp.actions.call refuses it. The app's own page calls such a route with fetch, which sends the session cookie.
- A signed route reads the declared header as t=<unix seconds>,n=<nonce>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256>. The MAC is keyed with the secret and covers t, the nonce, the method, the path, the canonical query string and the raw body, joined by newlines. The canonical query string is the pairs sorted by key, then value, written as application/x-www-form-urlencoded.
- The owner sets the secret with the secret_set admin tool before publishing. It never appears in actions.json, the Build Artifact or an export.
- GET /_littlebox/files/<id>, the path miniapp.files.url returns, answers a file the caller may read, with its own type. A person reads by the usual file rules, a visitor reads public files of a public app, and an API key reads the visibilities the owner named on it. A visitor without a session on a private app gets 401 authentication-required before any file is looked up; every other caller who may not read the file gets 404 File not found, the same as for a missing or deleted one.
- The editor preview serves no routes. Run them on a Development Kernel with littlebox dev, or on a Deployment.

Declared with `http` in `actions.json`. { "method": "GET" | "POST", "path": "/api/items", "signature"?: { "header": "X-Signature", "secret": "items_webhook" }, "callers"?: ["signature" | "key" | "session"] } on an action declared anonymous. GET binds a query and maps the query string onto its input bindings by type; POST binds a mutation and reads a JSON object body. callers names who may call the route; without it a signed route takes the signature or an API key, an unsigned route on a private Deployment an API key or a session, and an unsigned route on a public Deployment anyone. An action whose route does not answer anyone answers only on that route, never through miniapp.actions.call. The route answers { result } with the rows or { changes, lastInsertId }, and { error } with a status code. The Validation Gate and the Kernel refuse the same declarations with the same messages.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Action <name> must bind GET for a query and POST for a mutation.` | the method does not match the action's kind, or is neither GET nor POST | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> is authenticated, so it cannot declare http. Only anonymous actions answer on an HTTP route.` | the action's access is authenticated | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> has an invalid http path. Use a leading "/" and segments of letters, digits, ".", "_", "~" or "-", up to 200 characters.` | the path is "/", ends with "/", climbs with "..", or carries a query string | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> binds the reserved path <key>. Paths under /_littlebox, /oauth, /.well-known and /mcp belong to the Kernel.` | the first segment is reserved, in any letter case | Kernel | Same |
| `Actions <name> and <name> both bind <key>.` | two actions declare the same method and path | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> has an invalid signature header.` | the header is not 1 to 64 letters, digits and -, or is Authorization, Cookie, Host, Content-Type or Content-Length | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> names an invalid signature secret. Use lowercase letters, digits and "_", starting with a letter.` | the secret is not a secret name | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> has an invalid http binding.` | http is not an object, has another key, or its signature has a key other than header and secret | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> has an invalid callers list. List one or more of "signature", "key" and "session", each once.` | callers is not a list, is empty, repeats a caller or names another one | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> lists "signature" among its callers but declares no signature.` | callers names signature and the binding has no signature | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> declares a signature, so its callers must include "signature".` | the binding has a signature and callers leaves it out | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> signs with the secret <name>, which is not set for this project. Set it with secret_set before publishing.` | publishing, and the owner has not set the secret; the editor cannot see secrets, so only the Kernel refuses this | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Actions <names> sign with the secret <name>, which is not set for this project. Set it with secret_set before publishing.` | publishing, and several actions sign with one secret the owner has not set | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Actions <names> sign with the secrets <names>, which are not set for this project. Set each with secret_set before publishing.` | publishing, and more than one secret is unset; one refusal names every action and every secret | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `invalid-signature` | a signed route gets no signature, a malformed one, or one whose MAC does not match (401) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `stale-timestamp` | a signature's t is more than 300 seconds from the Kernel's clock; checked before the MAC, so it says nothing about the secret (401) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `authentication-required` | a route that takes an API key or a session, and no signature, gets neither (401) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `This route does not accept API keys.` | the route's callers leave out key and the request carries one (403) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `An API key works only on the app's HTTP routes and its file read path. The runtime endpoint takes an app session.` | a request to the runtime endpoint carries an API key (403) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `replayed-signature` | the same signature arrives a second time; a retry signs again with a new nonce (409) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `invalid-api-key` | Authorization carries an lbk_ key that is unknown or revoked (401) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `This API key may not call <name>.` | the key does not name the route's action (403) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `No route accepts POST on this path.` | a POST reaches a path no action binds (405) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `A route does not answer HEAD. Send GET.` | a HEAD reaches a path a query binds; it is refused before any SQL, with Allow: GET (405) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `The request body exceeds 64 KiB.` | a POST body is larger (413) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `The request body must be a JSON object.` | a POST body does not parse as JSON (400) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Repeated query parameter: <key>` | a GET names one input twice (400) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `rate-limited` | a caller exceeds the action limits of the runtime endpoint, or its address sent 10 unknown or revoked API keys to the Deployment in a minute (429, with Retry-After) | Kernel | Never refuses |

Limits:

- a POST body of 64 KiB
- a signature's t within 300 seconds of the Kernel's clock, a nonce of 1 to 64 letters, digits, - and _, and each signature accepted once
- the runtime endpoint's action rate limits: 30 per 10 seconds per client address without a key or session, 120 per 10 seconds per user or key
- 50 live API keys per Deployment
